title: A 45-day walk from Teknaf to Dhaka for hill children's schooling
excerpt: Uthwayngya Marma, who runs two schools in Bandarban for 260 children, is walking to raise support for a campus for 1,000 children in remote hill areas.

image.alt: Rengbook Para, a village in the hills of Bandarban
image.credit: File photo: S.H. Tanim / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

content:
A 12-member team began a 45-day walk from Teknaf to Dhaka on 19 November to draw attention to the lack of schooling for children in remote hill areas, The Daily Star reported. The "Walk for Humanity" plans to cover about 20 km a day through Cox's Bazar, Chattogram, Noakhali and Feni. The team reached Cox's Bazar town on 23 November. One member fell ill in Ukhiya.

The walk is led by Uthwayngya Marma from Lama upazila in Bandarban. He founded Rongkhedong Shishu Sadan in Lama in 2022 with nine children, and Prenrui Shikkhaloy in a border area of Alikadam in 2025. The two schools now support 260 disadvantaged, orphaned and vulnerable children. He sold land he inherited to keep them running.

Marma wants to build a campus with housing, education, food and health care for 1,000 children next year. He is asking 15,000 people to each give a sack of rice. "We want to ensure education, food and shelter for 1,000 children," he said.

Why it matters

Most families in the border areas are jhum farmers, many below the poverty line, and cannot send children to schools in upazila towns. Many villages have no school, and teachers are reluctant to serve there, so children drop out early. Local efforts like this one often fill gaps that government and NGO programmes do not reach, but they rarely get steady funding.
